rows.text: Eminence discounts OTHER Sphinx spells while The Ur-Sphinx is in the command zone or on the battlefield; it does not discount the commander itself. The mill-and-cast attack ability works only while the commander is on the battlefield. Develop discounted Sphinxes and card engines first, then deploy the commander when existing attackers can immediately turn it into free spells.

The refined list uses faster mana, precise reanimation, and cheap tribal enablers to make the attack plan more reliable. Its three Game Changers remain Consecrated Sphinx, Smothering Tithe, and Cyclonic Rift. This is a B-tier tribal attack and reanimation deck: it functions without resolving the nine-mana commander, but has no compact combo finish and still needs a board to win. Strong interactions do not eliminate that structural limit.

guide.title: Develop without waiting for nine mana

rows.name: The Ur-Sphinx
rows.text: A 10/10 flying finisher and a command-zone discount for the rest of the tribe. Its attack ability triggers once when one or more of your Sphinxes attack, not once per Sphinx. It need not attack itself, so casting it before attacking with an older Sphinx can immediately generate value.

For each resolving attack trigger, each player mills cards equal to the number of Sphinxes that attacked. You may cast up to one card milled this way from EACH player, including yourself, without paying its mana cost. In a four-player game that is up to four spells per trigger. More Sphinxes improve the choice of cards, rather than increasing the one-card-per-player allowance.

Cast those spells during the trigger's resolution; you cannot save the permission for later. Normal timing based on card type is ignored, but other restrictions and mandatory additional costs still apply. Lands cannot be cast, and an X in a free spell's mana cost is zero. New creatures from those spells do not join a combat whose attackers were already declared.

rows.name: Sol Ring + Thran Dynamo
rows.text: Accelerates the generic costs of your large creatures and artifacts. Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, and the three Talismans provide early color fixing; protect access to blue and do not mistake colorless acceleration for the white-blue-black needed to cast Raffine. Thran Dynamo: Four mana produces an immediate three-generic refund and three mana each later turn. This replaces a much slower untap payoff with actual acceleration toward the commander or two Sphinxes in one turn. Preserve enough colored sources; Dynamo cannot supply white, blue, or black.

rows.name: Urza's Incubator + Herald's Horn
rows.text: Choose Sphinx. It reduces Sphinx creature spells by two generic mana, including the commander. With Eminence, most other Sphinxes receive a combined three-mana generic discount. Herald's Horn: Another generic discount and a possible Sphinx card at each upkeep. The card goes to hand rather than being drawn. It is less explosive than Incubator but stays useful across a long game.

rows.name: Sapphire Medallion + Watcher of the Spheres
rows.text: Reduces generic costs of blue spells, including your commander, most Sphinxes, and several protective spells. It cannot reduce a colored mana requirement. Watcher of the Spheres: Reduces the generic cost of flying creature spells, including The Ur-Sphinx. It is not a Sphinx, so Eminence does not discount Watcher; Mirror Entity also normally lacks flying and gets no Watcher discount.

rows.name: Smothering Tithe
rows.text: A Game Changer that builds mana from opponents' draws when they decline to pay. It helps reach the commander while leaving mana for interaction and supports large Mirror Entity activations.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: Supplies cards, Treasure, and a 3/2 changeling that counts as a Sphinx. Each mode has a separate life cost: one for Treasure, two for drawing, three for the token. Choose only the modes you need; taking all three every turn costs six life.

rows.name: Tivit, Seller of Secrets
rows.text: Discounted to five mana by Eminence, it produces five voting outcomes in a normal four-player game because you vote twice. Your two votes can guarantee two Treasure tokens if you choose bribery; the opponents determine the other votes. Entry and combat-damage triggers supply mana or cards while building a flying threat.

guide.title: Make every Sphinx repay its cost

rows.name: Unesh, Criosphinx Sovereign
rows.text: Another two-mana generic reduction, plus a four-card split whenever it or another Sphinx you control enters. You choose one pile for your hand and put the other into your graveyard, stocking reanimation and spell reuse. This is not drawing cards.

rows.name: Defiler of Dreams
rows.text: You may pay two life to reduce a blue permanent spell's blue requirement by one, and each blue permanent cast draws a card. It stacks with generic reductions but can consume significant life alongside your lands, Reanimate, and Black Market Connections.

rows.name: Consecrated Sphinx + Loran of the Third Path
rows.text: The second Game Changer gives optional draws whenever opponents draw. Resolve and track each trigger rather than drawing automatically; with Roaming Throne, each opposing draw can offer four cards. Loran of the Third Path: Removes an artifact or enchantment for three mana without waiting for multiple tribal discounts. Its later draw activation gives both you and a chosen opponent a card, which can also trigger Consecrated Sphinx and Smothering Tithe. Do not gift an opponent a card if that could hand them the interaction or win they need.

rows.name: Universal Automaton
rows.text: Eminence reduces this changeling's one-generic cost to zero. It is a Sphinx in every zone, so it triggers Unesh and Kindred Discovery on entry and counts for tribal attacks and Bloodline Bidding. It is excellent cheap fodder for Diabolic Intent or Victimize. A free 1/1 is not worth spending a card on without a relevant engine, sacrifice use, or attack plan.

rows.name: Kindred Discovery
rows.text: Choose Sphinx. Draws from your Sphinx entries and attacks, including changeling tokens. Roaming Throne does not double this enchantment's triggers. The draws are mandatory, so track library size on large reanimation turns.

rows.name: Roaming Throne
rows.text: Choose Sphinx as it enters. It becomes a Sphinx on the battlefield and doubles triggered abilities of your OTHER Sphinx creatures: Unesh, Tivit, Consecrated Sphinx, and the commander's attack ability are premium choices. It is a Golem spell on the stack, so Eminence does not discount casting it.

rows.name: Spark Double
rows.text: Copies a creature you control without being legendary. A second Unesh adds another discount and entry engine; a second Ur-Sphinx gives another attack trigger; copying a utility Sphinx repeats its entry ability where applicable. It is not a Sphinx spell while being cast and receives no Eminence discount.

rows.name: Mystic Remora + Esper Sentinel
rows.text: Early card access and a tax on opposing noncreature spells while you develop mana. Let it go when cumulative upkeep would prevent a necessary engine or protection play. Esper Sentinel: Early noncreature-spell draw pressure. Counters from Denzilore can increase its tax later, but it does not become a Sphinx unless Mirror Entity changes its types.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent
rows.text: Sacrifice a spare changeling, expendable support creature, or Sphinx of False Conclusions to find the exact missing card. The sacrifice is an additional cost and is not refunded if the spell is countered. False Conclusions leaves its token copy behind after dying, making that exchange particularly efficient.

rows.name: Quantum Riddler
rows.text: Warp costs only one blue with Eminence, drawing a card on entry and offering a second cast on a later turn after the warp exile. A warped Riddler leaves at the next end step, so it is temporary development rather than a lasting blocker. Its low-hand draw replacement helps rebuild when you have one or fewer cards in hand.

rows.name: Sphinx of False Conclusions
rows.text: A three-mana flash Sphinx with Eminence, attack-based looting, and a token replacement when the nontoken original dies. It is a resilient threat and useful Victimize sacrifice. Its token copy does not make another copy when that token dies.

guide.title: Turn selection into a lethal board

rows.name: Raffine, Scheming Seer
rows.text: Its attack trigger counts ALL your attacking creatures and makes one targeted attacker connive that many times as one connive instruction. Draw and discard that many cards, then put counters on the targeted attacker for the nonland cards discarded. It seeds the graveyard while improving an attacker. Eminence cannot discount its three colored mana symbols.

rows.name: Curator of Mysteries
rows.text: A cheap flying body under Eminence, with a scry trigger for each other card you discard or cycle. Raffine discarding three cards generates three separate scry triggers. Curator can cycle for blue when you need lands or a reanimation target in the graveyard.

rows.name: Denzilore Fatehold
rows.text: Each separate scry or surveil event puts a +1/+1 counter on every creature you control. With Raffine and Curator of Mysteries, multiple discarded cards can produce multiple team-wide pumps before combat damage. Scry 3 or surveil 4 is still only ONE event and therefore one Denzilore trigger.

rows.name: Sphinx of Foresight
rows.text: Its opening-hand reveal improves your first upkeep, and its recurring upkeep scry works with Denzilore. On the battlefield it is a four-power flier for three mana with Eminence.

rows.name: Phyrexian Metamorph
rows.text: For three mana and two life, copy the best creature or artifact already on the battlefield. A second Consecrated Sphinx or Magister Sphinx repeats a high-impact role; copying a mana artifact is useful when acceleration is missing. It is not a Sphinx spell on the stack, though it can enter as a Sphinx. Unlike Spark Double, it does not avoid the legend rule.

rows.name: Entomb
rows.text: One black mana puts the specific creature you want into the graveyard for Reanimate, Animate Dead, Necromancy, or tribal recovery. Unesh develops a lasting engine; Magister Sphinx sets up a kill; Consecrated Sphinx supplies cards. This costs a card without giving a creature immediately, so plan the reanimation and protect against graveyard exile.

rows.name: Necromancy
rows.text: Another efficient reanimation effect from any graveyard. During your main phase it keeps the creature as long as the Aura remains. Casting it when sorcery timing was unavailable creates a sacrifice at the next cleanup step; that flash mode is for an urgent entry effect or blocker. It does not make a reanimated creature satisfy a cast-only condition.

When Raffine, Kindred Discovery, and The Ur-Sphinx all trigger from an attack, choose the order deliberately. Drawing the top card before milling can remove the card you meant to cast for free; discarding through Raffine can trigger Curator of Mysteries and let you scry before the commander's mill. Targets for triggered abilities are chosen when those abilities are put on the stack.

guide.title: Reuse what you discard and mill

rows.name: Reanimate
rows.text: Returns a creature from any graveyard for one black mana, at a life cost equal to its mana value. It can recover your expensive Sphinx or steal an opponent's creature that was milled. Reanimating The Ur-Sphinx costs nine life and only works if the commander is actually in the graveyard.

rows.name: Animate Dead
rows.text: Two-mana reanimation from any graveyard. The returned creature depends on the Aura remaining on the battlefield and gets -1/-0. Giving the creature protection from black with Akroma's Will causes the Aura to fall off, which makes you sacrifice the creature; indestructible does not prevent that sacrifice.

rows.name: Victimize
rows.text: Requires two creature cards already in your graveyard and a creature to sacrifice when it resolves. Exchange a changeling token or Sphinx of False Conclusions for two major threats. Both returns enter tapped, so they cannot attack or serve as untapped blockers immediately.

rows.name: Bloodline Bidding
rows.text: Choose Sphinx to rebuild your entire Sphinx graveyard, including Mirror Entity. Convoke lets surviving creatures help pay the eight-mana cost; this is not automatically cheap after a complete board wipe. Roaming Throne and Spark Double are not Sphinx cards in the graveyard and are not returned by choosing Sphinx.

rows.name: Scholar of the Lost Trove
rows.text: Its entry ability casts an instant, sorcery, or artifact from your graveyard for free. Bloodline Bidding can rebuild the tribe, while a spent removal spell can answer the obstacle stopping combat. Instants and sorceries cast this way are exiled afterward, so this is not a repeatable two-card reanimation loop.

rows.name: Sphinx of Forgotten Lore
rows.text: Flash lets you deploy it while preserving interaction. Attacking grants flashback to an instant or sorcery already in your graveyard. You must choose that target when its trigger goes on the stack, so you cannot select a card that the commander's pending trigger has not milled yet.

rows.name: Uldaros Theorix
rows.text: Its entry ability requires that you CAST it. Reanimating it does not provide the spell-copy payoff; casting it free through the commander does. It exiles up to one nonland card of each card type from your graveyard, then lets you cast copies with total mana value at most six. A copied Reanimate plus Arcane Signet fits; you cannot simply select several sorceries.

rows.name: Conspiracy Unraveler
rows.text: Turns expendable graveyard cards with total mana value ten into an alternative payment for a spell. It can help cast the commander from the command zone, but additional costs such as commander tax still apply. Exiling a precious reanimation target may be worse than paying mana normally.

rows.name: Takenuma, Abandoned Mire
rows.text: An untapped black land early, or late recovery of a creature to hand after milling three. Returning Uldaros to hand preserves the chance to cast it for its payoff.

Normally leave the commander in the command zone until its cost is manageable. If it dies while you have reanimation ready, you may leave it in the graveyard instead of moving it to the command zone. That exposes it to graveyard interaction, so make the choice based on the table and your available recovery.

guide.title: End the game with pressure and combat

rows.name: Magister Sphinx
rows.text: Sets a target player's life total to ten, turning your established fliers into an immediate lethal threat. This is particularly effective against life-gain decks. Roaming Throne doubles its entry trigger, potentially setting two opponents to ten; it is not an automatic kill without follow-up.

rows.name: Mirror Entity
rows.text: Changeling makes it a Sphinx in every zone, so Eminence reduces it to one generic and one white. Its activation changes your team's base power and toughness to X/X and gives all creature types. Use large mana reserves to turn small bodies into attackers; a small X can shrink your existing large Sphinxes.

Mirror Entity can make your non-Sphinx support creatures count toward the commander's attack trigger if activated BEFORE attackers are declared. It does not grant flying by itself. Existing +1/+1 counters still apply on top of its new base power and toughness. Do not activate for zero casually, and do not shrink your large Sphinxes without a reason.

rows.name: Crashing Drawbridge
rows.text: An early blocker that turns later creature deployment or mass reanimation into an immediate attack. It must have been under your control since the start of your turn, or have haste from Lightning Greaves, before using its tap ability. Activate after all the relevant creatures enter: its haste grant only affects the creatures you control as that activation resolves.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: Double strike turns a developed flying board into a fast finish, while its defensive mode supplies lifelink, indestructible, and protection from each color. With the commander actually under your control, choose both modes. Remember the Animate Dead interaction and that protection does not stop sacrifice or untargeted exile.

The commander's printed ten power with double strike is only twenty commander damage, not lethal from an untouched commander-damage total. One +1/+1 counter raises that above twenty-one. Ordinary life-total damage from several Sphinxes is usually the main route to victory.

rows.name: Dream Trawler
rows.text: Lifelink repairs the costs of your lands and black engines. Draws increase its power that turn, so its own attack draw and Kindred Discovery can make it a substantial attacker. Its discard-for-hexproof ability taps it; activating after it has attacked does not remove it from combat.

guide.title: Protect your advantage and remove blockers

rows.name: Reconnaissance
rows.text: Lets you attack for triggers, then remove a threatened attacker from combat and untap it before combat damage. It can also untap surviving attackers during the end-of-combat step after damage. The already-triggered commander ability remains on the stack, but a creature removed before damage does not deal combat damage.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: Haste can add an immediate commander attack or let a newly cast Sphinx contribute to the attack count. Shroud blocks your own targeted abilities too, including Raffine's connive target, Reconnaissance, and Clever Concealment. Move Greaves first when your own targeting matters.

rows.name: Clever Concealment
rows.text: Phases selected nonland permanents out through destruction or exile wipes, including your enchantment engines. Attached Auras and Equipment phase with their creatures rather than falling off. Convoke uses untapped creatures; your attackers usually cannot help pay after attacking.

rows.name: Force of Negation
rows.text: Free interaction on opponents' turns protects development before the nine-mana commander is on the battlefield. It counters only noncreature spells and exiles the countered spell. On your own turn, budget one generic and two blue; it is not a free shield for your finishing turn.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares
rows.text: Efficient exile for a must-answer creature. Anguished Unmaking covers nonland permanents more broadly at a three-life cost, which matters when you are already paying for cards and reanimation.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: Answers any counterable spell and supplies generic mana later for a major Sphinx or artifact. Swan Song, Dovin's Veto, and An Offer You Can't Refuse provide cheaper protection against noncreature spells; their coverage and drawbacks differ.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: The third Game Changer clears opponents' nonland boards for a finishing attack or answers a single obstacle for two mana. Overload preserves your board but does not remove lands.

rows.name: Toxic Deluge
rows.text: The reset when opponents develop faster than you. Choose X carefully: it can kill your own Sphinxes and costs life, but can also clear smaller creatures while preserving large fliers. Indestructible does not stop the toughness reduction.

rows.name: Enigma Thief
rows.text: If one of your Sphinxes or Rogues dealt combat damage to a player this turn, prowl becomes available. Eminence reduces that alternative cost to two generic and one blue. Its entry bounces up to one opposing nonland permanent per opponent, helping you keep pressure while interacting.

rows.name: Sphinx Summoner
rows.text: Searches an artifact creature to hand: Magister Sphinx for a lethal setup, Roaming Throne for doubled triggers, Phyrexian Metamorph for a flexible copy, Crashing Drawbridge for haste, or Universal Automaton for a free Sphinx entry. It cannot search every Sphinx merely because they share a creature type.

rows.name: Soul-Guide Lantern
rows.text: Controls opponents' graveyards without exiling your own, which is important when the commander is feeding graveyards. Hold it against a recursion response or sacrifice for a card when graveyard hate is irrelevant. You cannot activate it in the middle of the commander's resolving trigger.

guide.title: Find the engine or the finishing attack

rows.name: Entomb -> Unesh, Criosphinx Sovereign
rows.text: With cheap reanimation available, get the tribe's best cost-reduction and card-selection engine onto the battlefield ahead of its normal curve. Have a follow-up Sphinx ready so the entry trigger is not the entire turn.

rows.name: Entomb -> Magister Sphinx
rows.text: Use this when a player at ten life is within reach of your existing fliers. If you can copy or double the entry trigger, set up more than one opponent rather than repeatedly targeting the same player.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent -> Akroma's Will
rows.text: Find the finishing spell when the board is already wide enough. You need the commander on the battlefield to choose both modes; otherwise choose the mode that actually makes the attack lethal or safe.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent -> Clever Concealment
rows.text: Find protection when a board wipe would erase your advantage. Convoke can use creatures with summoning sickness but needs them untapped, so do not attack with everything before holding up a convoke defense.

rows.name: Sphinx Summoner -> Crashing Drawbridge
rows.text: Find haste before the rebuilding turn. If Drawbridge itself comes back in the same mass-reanimation event, it cannot tap immediately without a separate haste source; Lightning Greaves can supply that.

rows.name: Sea Gate Restoration
rows.text: A blue land when development requires one, with the option to pay three life to enter untapped. Late, its spell face refills based on the hand you have after casting it and removes the hand-size limit. Watch remaining library size when other draw engines are active.

cards.name: Sea Gate Restoration // Sea Gate, Reborn

rows.name: Unesh, Criosphinx Sovereign + Universal Automaton
rows.text: Unesh's entry already provides one four-card split; following with the free Sphinx gives another. The hand and graveyard both advance. This is finite card advantage, not an infinite loop.

rows.name: Phyrexian Metamorph + Magister Sphinx
rows.text: Reuse the life-setting entry effect for another opponent. Metamorph is also an artifact, so Sphinx Summoner can find it, and if it dies while copying a creature it reverts to its own characteristics in the graveyard.

Keep three lands with early blue and a route to the other colors, plus a rock or reducer and a useful early Sphinx or draw engine. A two-land hand needs reliable cheap card access and acceleration. Mulligan hands full of six- to eight-mana Sphinxes with no development, even with Eminence.

Your first goal is a working mana and card engine, usually a rock into a discounted Sphinx, Unesh, or another repeatable source of cards. You do not need to cast the commander early for the deck to function; its command-zone reduction is already doing work.

The mana base has 36 lands plus Sea Gate Restoration, with nine fetchlands, original duals, shocklands, one typed surveil land, and Raffine's Tower. Adarkar Wastes and Seachrome Coast improve early untapped blue access over additional surveil lands. Fetch for the next two spells: most Sphinxes need blue and Dream Trawler also needs double white. Three basics provide a modest fallback.

rows.name: Cavern of Souls
rows.text: Choose Sphinx to make actual Sphinx creature spells uncounterable, including Mirror Entity. It cannot provide colored mana for Spark Double or Roaming Throne merely because they will become Sphinxes later.

rows.name: Three Tree City
rows.text: Choose Sphinx. Its colored-mana ability needs two mana and its tap, so calculate the net gain from the number of Sphinxes you control. It is not an early three-color land. Otawara provides a channel answer when its land slot is no longer needed.

Reanimate and Animate Dead can use opponents' creatures too, but maintain enough life and interaction to survive the turn cycle. Hold a recovery spell when a wipe is likely instead of committing every threat.

On the finishing turn, resolve relevant pumps or protection before relying on them, order attack triggers deliberately, and remember that opponents may respond after the commander trigger has finished casting its free spells. Free does not mean uncounterable, and extra milling is also extra graveyard fuel for your opponents.
